tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who is a software engineer simulated closing each NYC subway stop using MTA trip data and found that closing the Third Avenue L stop would save riders significant time. He said only about 5% of riders at that stop board or alight, that the stop is not a transfer station, and that it is not wheelchair accessible. He estimated closing it would save about 1,800 hours daily even after counting walking time as twice as costly. Action: Ask the transportation committee to consider the proposal and explore a pilot closure of the stop with the MTA.

tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and delivery worker congestion
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on the sidewalk and street around 11th Street, obstructing businesses, residents, and landlords and raising fire-hazard concerns. Elected officials and the district manager said the bikes are kept in one spot because spread-out bikes were stolen, and that there are not enough legal corrals. The precinct plans an enforcement action on October 7 to confiscate improperly parked bikes, and community groups asked for tagging and notice instead, with multilingual outreach to workers. Action: Ensure the precinct and agencies carry out enforcement compassionately, provide multilingual notice to workers, and work with the community groups and elected officials to find legal parking or corral sites.

tickets.title: Seward Park drug activity and dark park lighting
tickets.summary: Residents and park users report increased drug use, homelessness, and needle debris in Seward Park, and the Seward Park Conservancy and the Lower East Side Ecology Center say drug users frequent a bathroom next to their building. A resident also noted poor lighting and dark spots in the park that let drug use go unseen. The district manager said a police task force is stationed there and that outreach providers are active, and asked about expanding mobile crisis teams. Action: Follow up with the Seventh Precinct and the Parks Department on drug activity and the need for lighting repairs, and ask residents to report out-of-service lights through 311.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for school council elections
tickets.summary: The board considered a resolution supporting a mobile voting option for Community Education Council elections because turnout has been around 2% and many households rely only on smartphones. Speakers noted that CEC demographics are skewed toward affluent schools and that immigrant families may fear data sharing, so outreach must clearly explain eligibility and privacy. The resolution would also urge the Office of Family and Community Empowerment to conduct more multilingual outreach. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education with a request for multilingual outreach and clear privacy messaging.

tickets.title: 11 Allen Street liquor license denial recommendation
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with 9 abstentions for a straight denial of the SLA application for 11 Allen Street by an operator formerly tied to Time Cafe near Forsyth and Canal Streets. Members cited the location's saturation, the prior location's problems, the lack of an unlicensed-location precedent, and crowds outside Time Cafe, while the committee had earlier proposed a compromise with reduced hours and no DJs. Because the board's recommendation does not bind the SLA, the speakers said the applicant could receive a license without stipulations unless community members attend the SLA hearing. Action: Organize community members and staff to attend the SLA hearing and seek elected official support for the denial recommendation.

tickets.title: August SLA resolution wording corrections for items three and ten
tickets.summary: The chair reported two clerical errors in the August SLA resolutions. Item 10, Softours Tea House, should read as a denial of a beer and wine license unless stipulations are agreed to, not a full on-premises license. Item 3, Cozy Cafe, should likewise read as a denial of a beer and wine license. Action: Correct the August resolutions for items three and ten to state beer and wine licenses and send the corrected versions to the SLA.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP timing and resolution follow-up
tickets.summary: The joint land use and economic development committee meeting on the Essex Market request for proposals found EDC unprepared to explain how the board's two resolutions were incorporated. The RFP was supposed to be issued by the end of the month, and the board's resolutions asked EDC to keep the market community-focused and postpone issuance. A follow-up meeting with EDC was planned, which will not be open to the public but will be reported back. Action: Hold the follow-up meeting with EDC and seek a postponement of the RFP so the board's resolution requirements can be included.

tickets.title: Free public restroom pilot placement and access rules
tickets.summary: The city is installing 17 free public restrooms citywide as a one-year pilot, with two in the district, including one near Delancey Plaza and one at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. DOT leads the installation, and a contractor will maintain the restrooms, which are expected to go in around mid-October. The board raised concerns about access rules, emergency calls, and who can use the facilities. Action: Bring a resolution next month that sets out the board's requirements for access, emergency response, and oversight during the pilot.

tickets.title: Canal Street redesign and Manhattan Bridge exits letter
tickets.summary: The transportation committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT reiterating community concerns about the Manhattan Bridge exits, especially after a recent fatal crash. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project, which has not had an update since January. Action: Follow up with DOT and the mayor's office for a response on the Manhattan Bridge exits and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing effects on FDR Drive follow-up
tickets.summary: A member asked whether the congestion pricing impacts projected for the FDR Drive in the air quality report actually materialized. The member also asked whether MTA or DOT plans to return to the board to report on congestion effects. The chair said this was not on the committee's list but could be followed up. Action: Request a report from MTA or DOT on actual congestion impacts on the FDR Drive and whether further reporting is planned.

tickets.title: NYCHA residents food, necessities, and deaf communication access
tickets.summary: A public speaker described long-running struggles of NYCHA residents with food, water, necessities, and work access, and asked what the community could do. He also raised the need for communication access for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents, using an interpreter during his comments. He wants drugs and toxicity removed from the community. Action: Refer the NYCHA food, necessities, and communication access concerns to the appropriate agencies and check on the status of assistance for residents.

tickets.title: Roller skating rink proposal on East River Pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: A speaker proposed a 300,000 square foot, three-story, multi-use indoor roller skating facility on the East River pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall to replace lost rinks. The proposal includes $8 admission with skate rental, and projects 250 to 400 direct jobs. Action: Refer the pier development proposal to the land use committee for review and possible follow-up with the proposer.

tickets.title: Housing plan market-rate share and affordable housing priority
tickets.summary: The city draft housing plan proposes a little over 7,000 units in five years, but 75% are market rate, which conflicts with the board's top need of affordable housing. The board commented only briefly because the turnaround was short. Members said land use committees need to take positions proactively because comment periods are getting shorter. Action: Have the land use committee develop proactive positions that prioritize affordable housing in future housing plan comments.

tickets.title: October district needs and budget priority rankings
tickets.summary: The district manager reported that the board will vote in October on district needs and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for city agencies. Committees will develop priorities, and district managers are meeting with agencies to learn about cuts and vacancies. The example given was summer youth employment, where the board should ask how many youth were turned away. Action: Have each committee complete its ranked expense and capital priorities for the October vote.

tickets.title: Bylaws revision on attendance and removal process
tickets.summary: The board reviewed proposed bylaw changes that would create an attendance process with a letter and executive committee meeting before any removal recommendation. The changes would also remove attendance from the main removal process and require public members to follow conflict of interest policies. A member raised concern that the proposal makes the recommendation process double-layered. Action: Vote on the bylaw revisions at the October full board meeting after the required 28-day notice.

tickets.title: Board training on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures
tickets.summary: The board chair announced planned trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, with dates to be announced later. The chair said these would help new members and serve as refreshers for others. The chair asked members to email requests for training topics. Action: Schedule the SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures trainings and report out dates to members.

tickets.title: MetroCard support for immigrant center visitors
tickets.summary: A community member asked whether transportation costs such as MetroCards or OMNY fares could be offset for residents traveling to the new Manhattan Immigrant Welcome Center at 431 West 125th Street. He noted the trip from lower Manhattan often requires multiple transfers and takes about an hour. The liaison said the question would be raised with the office. Action: Raise the MetroCard or OMNY fare support question with the elected official's office and report back on whether transportation costs can be offset.
